CK-01.plain: Try the project's model yourself in Ollama in about 2 minutes. This is a demo; it checks nothing.
CK-01.developer: `ollama run ryoari/openverifiablellm` — GGUF via llama.cpp; outputs close to PyTorch but not bit-identical; not a verification.

CK-02.plain: A 10-minute consistency check you run, no GPU: it shows the release matches the project's timestamped record. No training is recomputed.
CK-02.developer: README Getting started block (lines 156-167, verbatim): pip install, hf download, sha256sum -c, openssl ts -verify, clone --branch v1.0.1, ovl.py verify.

CK-03.plain: For the consistency check, use ovl.py from the project's v1.0.1 tag. It fails if anchor.json is missing.
CK-03.developer: Use ovl.py from tag v1.0.1; the download's code/ copy predates the anchor check.

CK-04.plain: When you run the consistency check, a pass prints: the chain head matches (38 entries) and the weights match chain entry 37.
CK-04.developer: Expected lines '# anchor anchor.json: chain head MATCH (38 entries)' and '# weights conversation-model.pt: MATCH chain entry 37'.

CK-05.plain: Actual verification you run, about 1 hour: the project's RunPod template recomputes one segment bit for bit on an RTX 5090.
CK-05.developer: RunPod template mai1ozh35g runs simple/checker_pod.sh; ~22 GB download + ~20 min training; prints one result line.

CK-06.plain: Renting the GPU for that hour costs about US$1–1.50, per the project's docs. Prices change.
CK-06.developer: about US$1–1.50 (RTX 5090 list price US$1.19/h at the time).

CK-07.plain: Or run the project's verify_segment.sh yourself: one random segment (about 20 minutes), three random ones, or your choice.

CK-08.plain: You can check both timestamps on the project's record yourself with openssl.

VE-01.plain: Coverage map: {total} tiles, one per segment. The project checked all {matched} and all matched. Independent checks: none yet.
VE-01.developer: Tiles = verifications.jsonl rows 1-37 (project second pod), segments 0-36; label 'project'; reserve 'independent'.

VE-02.plain: Segment k means the training between boundary k and boundary k+1 in the project's record.
VE-02.developer: segment k = boundary k → k+1; passes only if recomputed state is identical to entry k+1.

VE-03.plain: There are {rows} check results, all matches, all run by the project: {second} second machine, {training} training machine, {fresh} fresh machine.
VE-03.developer: verifications.jsonl: 46 rows = 37 'project second pod' + 8 'project training pod' (22,31-36, 5 fast loader) + 1 'project fresh machine public files only' (21).

VE-04.plain: The project also recomputed segment 21 on a fresh machine using only public files. It matched. Not an independent check.
VE-04.developer: verifications.jsonl row 46: segment 21, 'project fresh machine public files only', verify_segment.sh from the release.

VE-06.plain: How likely independent random checks catch one forged segment: 1 − ((N−1)/N)^M. So far only the project has checked.
VE-06.developer: P(detect) = 1 − ((N−1)/N)^M; one checker doing k distinct segments: k/N.

VE-07.plain: {m95} independent random checks of {total} segments would catch one forged segment 95% of the time. Only the project has checked.
VE-07.developer: Smallest M with p≥0.95 at N={total} is {m95} (p=0.95090).

VE-08.plain: {m99} independent random checks would give a 99% chance. So far only the project has checked.
VE-08.developer: Smallest M with p≥0.99 at N={total} is {m99} (p=0.99025).

VE-09.plain: Independent checks so far: 0. Every check to date was run by the project.
VE-09.developer: count(checker not starting 'project') = 0 across both verifications.jsonl files.

VE-10.plain: Check results, including the project's own, are self-reported text lines. They are unsigned, and random segment choice is unproven.

VE-11.plain: On the project's roadmap, not built yet: signed check results and segment choice from public randomness.
VE-11.developer: Roadmap: signed check results + segment choice from public randomness.
